usageNotes: Use this before adding or updating a PBS remote to verify its TLS certificate. If the host's certificate is not already trusted (e.g., it is self-signed), the API returns the certificate details so you can capture the fingerprint for use in subsequent remote-add or remote-update calls. Requires the System.Modify privilege at the root path.

examples.summary: Probe a self-signed PBS remote to retrieve its certificate fingerprint

tips: If the certificate is already trusted by the system's CA bundle, the response body is null — a non-error empty response is the success case for trusted certs.
When the cert is untrusted, the returned fingerprint should be copied and passed as the 'fingerprint' field when registering the remote, completing the trust-on-first-use (TOFU) flow.
The hostname field accepts an optional port (e.g., host:8007); omit the port to default to PBS's standard 8007.
API tokens are supported (allowtoken: true), so a scoped token with System.Modify is sufficient — no interactive session required.
